From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin dēlīrāre. By surface analysis, delírio +‎ -ar.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /de.liˈɾa(ʁ)/ [de.liˈɾa(h)]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /de.liˈɾa(ʁ)/ [de.liˈɾa(h)]
    • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /de.liˈɾa(ɾ)/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /de.liˈɾa(ʁ)/ [de.liˈɾa(χ)]
    • (Caipira) IPA(key): /de.liˈɾa(ɻ)/
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /dɨ.liˈɾaɾ/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /dɨ.liˈɾaɾ/
    • (Southern Portugal) IPA(key): /dɨ.liˈɾa.ɾi/

  • Hyphenation: de‧li‧rar

Verb

[edit]

delirar (first-person singular present deliro, first-person singular preterite delirei, past participle delirado)

  1. (intransitive) to be delirious (in the state of delirium)

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin dēlīrāre.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /deliˈɾaɾ/ [d̪e.liˈɾaɾ]
  • Rhymes: -aɾ
  • Syllabification: de‧li‧rar

Verb

[edit]

delirar (first-person singular present deliro, first-person singular preterite deliré, past participle delirado)

  1. (intransitive) to be delirious
